title: African American Civil Rights Network Act of 2017
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on July 26, 2017. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

African American Civil Rights Network Act of 2017

(Sec. 3) This bill requires the Department of the Interior to establish within the National Park Service (NPS) a U.S. Civil Rights Network that encompasses: (1) all NPS units and programs that relate to the African American civil rights movement from 1939 through 1968; (2) with the property owner's consent, other federal, state, local, and privately owned properties that relate or have a verifiable connection to such movement and that are included in, or eligible for, the National Register of Historic Places; and (3) other governmental and nongovernmental facilities and programs of an educational, research, or interpretive nature that are directly related to such movement.

In carrying out the network, Interior must: (1) review civil rights movement studies and reports, such as the Civil Rights Framework Study; (2) produce and disseminate educational materials relating to such movement; (3) provide technical assistance; and (4) adopt an official, uniform symbol or device for the Network and issue regulations for the symbol's use.

The network shall expire seven years after enactment of this bill.

summary.headline: A 2018 law directs the National Park Service to set up a U.S. Civil Rights Network that links sites and programs about the African American civil rights movement from 1939 to 1968.
summary.what_it_does: The law requires the Department of the Interior to create a network within the National Park Service. It covers National Park Service sites and programs tied to the African American civil rights movement from 1939 through 1968, and it can include other historic properties and educational or research facilities. Interior must review existing civil rights studies, produce and share educational materials, offer technical help, and adopt an official symbol for the network with rules for its use. The network expires seven years after enactment.

who_it_affects.group: National Park Service and Department of the Interior
who_it_affects.how: They must set up and run the network, review civil rights studies, create educational materials, provide technical assistance, and set rules for an official symbol.

who_it_affects.group: Owners of historic properties related to the civil rights movement
who_it_affects.how: Privately owned, state, local, and other federal properties that are listed or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places can be included only with the owner's consent.

who_it_affects.group: Museums, schools, and research or educational facilities
who_it_affects.how: Facilities whose work directly relates to the civil rights movement may be included in the network as educational, research, or interpretive sites.

who_it_affects.group: Visitors interested in civil rights history
who_it_affects.how: They may find more educational materials and linked sites that document the 1939 to 1968 movement.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on January 8, 2018, and the network is set to expire seven years after that date, around January 2025.
